'''Keith Fagnou''' (June 27, 1971 &ndash; November 11, 2009) was a [[Canadians|Canadian]] [[organic chemist]] and studied education and was a professor of chemistry at [[University of Saskatchewan]] and associate professor of [[organic chemistry]] at the [[University of Ottawa]].  His research focused on developing new reactions that avoid unnecessary activation of substrates and that can instead directly functionalize C–H bonds of simple molecules and introduce C–C bonds.<ref name = "Fagnou">{{cite journal|journal= Chemical & Engineering News|volume=87|issue=50|pages=41–42|year=2009|doi=10.1021/cen-v087n050.p041|title=OBITUARIES|last= Ainsworth|first= Susan J.}}</ref>

==Biography==

Dr. Keith Fagnou was born on June 27, 1971, in [[Saskatoon]], [[Saskatchewan]].  Fagnou, a former naval reserve officer, pursued studies at the University of Saskatchewan and received a Bachelor of Education (B.Ed.) in 1995.  After teaching at the high school level for a short period, he continued his studies in chemistry at the [[University of Toronto]] in 1998 under the supervision of Mark Lautens. In 2000 he received his M.Sc. degree, and in 2002 his Ph.D.  Professor Lautens said that Keith "was exceptionally bright and exceptionally down-to-earth and was the most productive person, in the history of his research group."<ref>[https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/ottawa/ottawa-star-researcher-mourned-after-h1n1-death-1.861706 "Ottawa 'star' researcher mourned after H1N1 death"], ''[[CBC News]]'', Ottawa, 13 November 2009. Retrieved on 2009-3-8.</ref>   After his PhD, he joined the faculty at the [[University of Ottawa]] as an [[assistant professor]] and in 2007 was promoted to [[associate professor]] with [[tenure]] and awarded a University of Ottawa Research Chair in the Development of Novel [[Catalytic]] Transformations.<ref>[http://mysite.science.uottawa.ca/bliegaul/keith.html "Fagnou Research Group - About Keith"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304190913/http://mysite.science.uottawa.ca/bliegaul/keith.html |date=2016-03-04 }}, Retrieved on 2010-3-8.</ref>

While at the University of Ottawa, he established a research program primarily devoted to the development of novel "direct arylation" reactions which allow for the rapid synthesis of important building blocks in medicinal chemistry.<ref>[http://mysite.science.uottawa.ca/bliegaul/research.html "Fagnou Research Group - Research"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170315124212/http://mysite.science.uottawa.ca/bliegaul/research.html |date=2017-03-15 }}, Retrieved on 2010-3-8.</ref>  Of note, the development of direct arylation of [[benzene]]<ref name = "benzene">{{cite journal
| last = Lafrance
| first = M
| author2=Fagnou, K
| journal = J. Am. Chem. Soc.
| volume = 128
| pages = 16496–7
| year = 2006
| doi = 10.1021/ja067144j
| pmid = 17177387
| title = Palladium-catalyzed benzene arylation: incorporation of catalytic pivalic acid as a proton shuttle and a key element in catalyst design
| issue = 51
}}</ref> and pyridine N-oxide.<ref name = "pyridine">{{cite journal
| last = Campeau
| first = L.-C. |author2=Rousseaux, S. |author3=Fagnou, K
| journal = J. Am. Chem. Soc.
| volume = 127
| pages = 18020–1
| year = 2005
| doi = 10.1021/ja056800x
| pmid = 16366550
| title = A solution to the 2-pyridyl organometallic cross-coupling problem: regioselective catalytic direct arylation of pyridine N-oxides
| issue = 51
}}</ref>  Members of his research group are sometimes referred to as "The Fagnou Factory".<ref>Casey, D. [http://cnews.canoe.com/CNEWS/Canada/2009/11/12/11731241-sun.html "Popular professor dies of swine flu"]{{dead link|date=April 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}, ''[[The Ottawa Sun]]'', Ottawa. Retrieved on 2009-3-8.</ref>  His contributions in the field were rewarded with numerous awards and have been included in reviews published on the subject.<ref name = "Review">{{cite journal
| last = Ackermann
| first = L |author2=Vicente, R. |author3=Kapdi, A. R.
| journal = Angew. Chem. Int. Ed.
| volume = 48
| issue = 52
| pages = 9792–826
| year = 2009
| pmid = 19998294
| doi = 10.1002/anie.200902996
| title = Transition-Metal-Catalyzed Direct Arylation of (Hetero)Arenes by Cï£¿H Bond Cleavage
}}</ref>

Dr. Keith Fagnou died of complications resulting from a [[H1N1]] influenza infection on November 11, 2009, at the age of 38.<ref>Page, S. [https://ottawacitizen.com/technology/H1N1+suspected+death+professor/2216534/story.html "H1N1 suspected in death of U of O professor: Loss of father of three, 38, shocks scientists around the world"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091114120357/http://www.ottawacitizen.com/technology/H1N1+suspected+death+professor/2216534/story.html |date=2009-11-14 }}, ''[[The Ottawa Citizen]]'', Ottawa. 13 Novembre 2009. Retrieved on 2009-2-27.</ref>

The University of Ottawa established the "Keith Fagnou Scholarship in Science" in his memory.<ref>[http://www.science.uottawa.ca/assets/pdf/keith-fagnou-en.PDF "Keith Fagnou Scholarship in Science"]{{Dead link|date=October 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}, Retrieved on 2010-3-8.</ref>  The members of his research group also organized a symposium (KFOS) in his honour which was held May 5–7, 2010.<ref>[http://mysite.science.uottawa.ca/bliegaul/kfos_home_e.html "Keith Fagnou Organic Chemistry Symposium"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130130003544/http://mysite.science.uottawa.ca/bliegaul/kfos_home_e.html |date=2013-01-30 }}, Retrieved on 2010-2-27.</ref>  The Pacifichem chemistry conference also held a memorial symposium titled "C-H Functionalization, Memorial Symposium for Professor Keith Fagnou".<ref>[http://www.pacifichem.org/symposia/c_symp_18.htm "PACIFICHEM 2010"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100224033942/http://www.pacifichem.org/symposia/c_symp_18.htm |date=2010-02-24 }}, Retrieved on 2010-3-9.</ref>  In 2011, Keith was recognized as the #77 chemist in the world over the period 2000-2010 on the basis of citations per paper, according to Thomson-Reuters' Sciencewatch.com.<ref>[http://sciencewatch.com/dr/sci/misc/Top100Chemists2000-10/ "Top 100 Chemists, 2000-2010]</ref>
